main_text.p: ritus ꝑduci[?] potest. Nam ad illius procreatione duo maximè sunt necessaria, tenuisimus sanguis, & locus, ubi fit calidus. Sed in cerebri ventriculis nullus continetur sanguis nedum tenuis. Deinde ipsi ventriculi naturam cerebri, quæ frigida est, retinent. Nam cerebri temperamentum, quod secundum naturam est, frigidū esse oportere nullus ambigit medicus. Id enim passim often dit Galenus, & præfertim lib. de Temperamentis secundo. Unde sanguinem, qui in ipsius cerebri venis & arterijs habetur, pituitosum esse & frigidum, consentiunt omnes medici. His adde quod Aristot. suis in Problematis cerebri frigiditatem cordis calorem temperare, memoriæ mandauit. Postremò unicum esse animantis cuiuslibet spiritū, authoritate Galeni probari potest. Ipse enim libro de Simplicium MediCap.8. camentorum facultatibus quinto, spiritum nihil esse aliud, quàm innatum calidū perspicuis verbis exprimit: At unicū est innatum calidum. Unus igitur est duntaxat animalium spiritus. Idem confirmat Aristoteles libro de Generatione animalium capite ultimo, ubi unicum esse animantis spiritum, qui quidē sese sic habet in rebus á na-

page.notes: Long s in the scan is read as s throughout. Words such as "often" and "passim" in the Galen sentence are printed in the text as shown; "fecun / dum" is joined without a hyphen because no hyphen is printed at the line end. Doubtful: the mark before "pduci" (ꝑ?) and the letter "á" at the line end before "na-", which may be an abbreviation mark rather than a plain a. The word "præfertim" has an uncertain ligature over the æ. Printed "fpiritu" and "calidu" are kept as printed. Note the printed "dit" and "Ariftot" with long s, transcribed as s.
